correctness.rationale: For each fixed pattern, greedy matching gives independent geometric waiting times, and its probability generating function is multiplicative. The angular Fourier filter extracts exactly matching Parikh vectors. The first root U(r)=1 is unique; full-support positivity excludes competing unit-circle poles. Near the unique saddle the covariance matrix diag(v)-vv^T is positive definite with determinant prod(v), giving the exact Gaussian constant. A final (1-z)^(-1) convolution multiplies it by (1-r)^(-1). An independent exact rational computation checked 39,286 words and seven distributions, with further binary algebraic and uniform length-100 coefficient checks. Boundary q>=2 and all positive masses are explicit; no finite test substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: A classical Parikh-balanced pattern constraint yields an exact and nontrivial alphabet-codimension penalty n^{-(q-1)/2} in the expected count of DISTINCT scattered patterns, whereas the exponential growth rate remains that of all subsequences. The theorem gives a full-support bias-sensitive leading constant for every fixed alphabet size, a natural infinite-class answer that is distinct from contiguous-factor richness or fixed-length pattern tables.
